articles.title: What Is Eval-Driven Development? How to Improve AI Agents
articles.summary: Development on most agents starts the same way. You write a prompt, try a few questions by hand, adjust, and try again. This works well in the beginning, when agent errors are obvious and improvements are easy to see. But over time it becomes increasingly difficult to know whether your most recent change made an agent better or worse. Eval-driven development (EDD) solves this by giving you a consistent set of metrics to measure your agent’s performance against and guide your decision making. articles.title: Accelerate GPU training on Unity Catalog tables with UCDataset
articles.summary: GPUs are usually the most expensive part of any training run, and most teams can't keep them busy. The bottleneck usually isn't the model. It's getting data from where it lives to the GPU fast enough - and every second those chips sit waiting, you're burning both time and money. Today we're releasing the Unity Catalog Dataset (UCDataset) in Beta on AI Runtime. UCDataset is a native PyTorch data loader that streams Unity Catalog tables directly to every GPU in your training job, with no exports, no copies, and no custom loader code. articles.title: Do AI coding agents care about SemVer or is it something for humans only?
articles.summary: Semantic versioning tells developers how risky an upgrade is. A patch fixes bugs, a minor release adds features without breaking anything and a major release breaks things, so you know how closely to look before you upgrade. On paper, that signal is redundant when an AI coding agent does the upgrade. The agent has no muscle memory tied to the old API. It can read the new code and run the tests, so why would it care what the version number says? We suspected it wouldn’t, and that SemVer had become something only people need. articles.title: Show HN: MemSeal – provenance containment for agent long-term memory
articles.summary: MemSeal: a deterministic provenance-tracking containment layer on the write/recall boundary of AI agent long-term memory (GATE 2 self-reported FAIL; evaluation only). MemSeal is a containment layer on the write/recall boundary of an AI agent's long-term memory. Every memory entry is wrapped in a provenance envelope (who wrote it, from what source, derived from what, at which trust tier) inside a SHA-256 hash chain.
